samples.summary: `basenamed` does not mirror react-router's `pathname === "/"` special case, so the same-page exemption misfires at the app root under a basename
samples.evidence: react-router v7's `useNavigate` does `path.pathname = path.pathname === "/" ? basename : joinPaths([basename, path.pathname])`. `basenamed` implements only the `joinPaths` half: `["/app", "/"].join("/").replace(/\/\/+/g, "/")` yields `"/app/"`, while the push carries `"/app"`. So when the current location is the root under a non-"/" basename, `leaving()` compares `"/app"` !== `"/app/"` and reports true for a navigation that never leaves the page — a spurious prompt, and (via the same pathname comparison at line 191) it also affects when an open prompt is considered stale. The new basename test only exercises a non-root path, where the special case does not apply.

samples.summary: A second navigation attempted while a prompt is open is silently swallowed — neither performed nor reported
samples.evidence: In `push`, when a guard holds the navigation and `pendingRef.current` is already set, the `if (!pendingRef.current)` block is skipped and the function `return`s. The caller (a `<Link>` handler, or a programmatic `navigate()` from e.g. a mutation `onSuccess`) has already `preventDefault`ed, so the navigation is dropped with no dialog, no error and no replay. The modal dialog blocks pointer-driven links, but programmatic navigations (query callbacks, timers, websocket-driven redirects) are not blocked by it.

samples.summary: Browser back/forward still discards unsent edits silently — the guard covers only `push` through the navigator
samples.evidence: The provider patches `UNSAFE_NavigationContext.navigator.push` only; the doc comment itself states "Browser back/forward is *not* covered: it arrives on the history listener, not here." `beforeunload` also does not fire for a popstate, so pressing Back from an editor with unsent edits unmounts `DocumentProvider` and drops the in-memory change queue with nothing said — the exact data-loss case the feature exists to prevent. Back is a very common way to leave a document reached from a list. Nothing in the change mitigates it (no `history.pushState` sentinel, no `useBlocker`, no data router).

samples.summary: Timer-released redirect latch can re-assign `window.location.href` every 2s while a navigation is still loading
samples.evidence: `redirectRelease` clears `isRedirecting` after a fixed `REDIRECT_LATCH_MS` regardless of whether the navigation was refused or is merely slow. JS keeps running until the new document commits, so on a slow `/login` load any 401 arriving after 2s re-assigns `window.location.href = '/login'`, cancelling and restarting the in-flight navigation. With recurring background requests (react-query refetch intervals, polling) after session expiry this repeats every 2 seconds indefinitely — including re-triggering the `beforeunload` prompt each time when the sync guard is armed.

samples.summary: Refs are mutated during render, so a discarded concurrent render can desynchronise `pendingRef` from the `prompt` state
samples.evidence: Lines 82 (`locationRef.current = location`) and 191-195 (clearing `pendingRef`/`promptPathRef` during render) are render-phase side effects. If React discards that render pass (interrupted concurrent render, or an offscreen/Suspense retry), the ref writes persist while the `prompt` state does not — leaving the dialog visible with `pendingRef.current === null`, so "Leave" (`run?.()`, line 202) silently does nothing and the user's navigation is dropped.

`redirectTo` returns early when `isRedirecting` is true, and the only place `isRedirecting` is cleared is the timer callback, which sets `redirectRelease = null` first. So past the early return `redirectRelease` is always `null` and the `clearTimeout` never runs.

samples.summary: A guard that throws aborts the navigation and propagates into the link click handler
samples.evidence: `const held = guard();` is not wrapped. A guard implementation that throws (e.g. `hasUnsentEdits()` touching a disposed Yorkie doc after an unmount race) both prevents `run()` from being reached and surfaces as an unhandled error from the `<Link>` click handler, leaving the user stuck on the page with no dialog.

finding.summary: Browser back/forward still discards unsent edits silently — the guard covers only `push` through the navigator
finding.evidence: The provider patches `UNSAFE_NavigationContext.navigator.push` only; the doc comment itself states "Browser back/forward is *not* covered: it arrives on the history listener, not here." `beforeunload` also does not fire for a popstate, so pressing Back from an editor with unsent edits unmounts `DocumentProvider` and drops the in-memory change queue with nothing said — the exact data-loss case the feature exists to prevent. Back is a very common way to leave a document reached from a list. Nothing in the change mitigates it (no `history.pushState` sentinel, no `useBlocker`, no data router).

verdict.reason: The factual absence is real — I confirmed repo-wide (not just packages/frontend/src) that no `popstate` handler, `useBlocker`, `history.pushState` sentinel, data router, or flush-on-unmount exists; `navigation-guard-provider.tsx:146-165` passes `go` and `replace` straight through and only wraps `push`. So there is no counterexample to cite. However it is not a blocking defect under the Correctness rubric: it is an explicitly declared scope boundary, not a logic or runtime error. The design doc carries it as a named entry in its own Risks and Mitigation register (`docs/design/sync-status.md:463-471`: "Browser back/forward is not guarded … both were judged out of proportion to the case, and this stays a known limitation"), repeated at :355-359, in the task doc at :31 and the lessons doc at :25-33, and in the provider's own doc comment at lines 55-61. The implemented `push` path contains no wrong condition, inverted logic, missing guard, async mistake, or broken invariant; `POP` behaves exactly as it did before the change, and the underlying loss traces to absence of local persistence, itself a stated Non-Goal (`sync-status.md:458-461`). "The mitigation should also cover scenario X" is a product/scope judgement the Correctness lens does not own.
